h1: Adrian View Resort Ko Si Chang — a small, quiet guesthouse near the Khao Khat viewpoint
intro: Picture this: you take the ferry across from Sriracha to Ko Si Chang, then check into a little house of just 7 rooms where the owner comes out to greet you herself. You open the door to a brightly coloured room with a balcony to catch the breeze, and around the house a small garden where butterflies drift past in the morning — Adrian View Resort is a small Bed & Breakfast guesthouse on Ko Si Chang island, Chonburi, that sells quiet and friendliness rather than luxury · what a lot of people mention is the privacy, the attentive owner, and the location near the Khao Khat viewpoint · open since around 2012 · from about ฿800/night, scored 8.5 on Trip.com and 4.3 out of 5 on TripAdvisor — a little place that suits travellers on a modest budget who want to escape the city and sleep somewhere quiet on the island.

body.html: Who Adrian View Resort is right for — the shortest way to put it is that Adrian View Resort is for people who want to get away from the bustle and sleep somewhere quiet on Ko Si Chang on a modest budget, and who aren't chasing luxury or a full set of facilities · it isn't a big resort with a pool, a gym, or a full day of activities, but a small Bed & Breakfast guesthouse of only about 7 rooms run by the owner, in Tha Thaewawong, Ko Si Chang, Chonburi · it has been open since around 2012, so it has been on the island long enough to build up a base of regulars who come back · the charm here lies in being simple and friendly rather than in numbers or fancy fittings · real reviews on Trip.com, Booking.com and TripAdvisor line up to say the people who suit this place are couples after a quiet one-night, two-day trip, solo travellers who like a calm atmosphere, and people who come to Ko Si Chang to rest slowly rather than to look for nightlife or a lively scene · those who expect a fancy room, a wide sea view from the balcony, a pool, or chain-hotel service may want to think twice, because Adrian View is a small guesthouse that sells comfort and calm above all · the picture from reviews is "a lovely little place, clean, kind owner, good value," which matches the crowd that comes to Ko Si Chang to genuinely rest rather than to do it all.

Location and getting there — Adrian View Resort sits on Ko Si Chang, a small island off the coast of Sriracha, Chonburi · part of the charm of getting here is that you have to take a ferry across, which is part of the island experience · from Bangkok, drive or take a coach to Koh Loy Pier in Sriracha, around an hour and a half to two hours, then board one of the scheduled passenger ferries, around 50 baht each way, with the crossing taking about 45 min · the address is 262/17 Moo 6, Tha Thaewawong, Ko Si Chang, Chonburi 20120 · the location's strong point is that Adrian View is close to the Khao Khat viewpoint and Laem Chakraphong, the highlights of Ko Si Chang, sitting just a few hundred metres from Khao Khat, with the town and pier a short walk away · some reviews note it is only a couple of hundred metres from the town and about a 7 min walk to the Ko Si Chang pier, which is handy for anyone not renting a vehicle on the island · on the island it's common to hire a skylab three-wheeler or a motorbike to ride around, making it easy to stop at viewpoints such as Chong Khao Khat, Phra Chudadhuj Palace, and the Chao Pho Khao Yai Shrine · one thing to note: the last ferry back to the mainland is usually in the evening, so check the ferry timetable in advance, especially on weekdays, and on long weekends the boats can get full enough that you'll wait for the next one, so always allow extra travel time.

"A small place, very quiet, close to Khao Khat so it's an easy walk over to take photos. The owner is kind and comes out to chat and recommend places to visit · the room is clean, sleep is comfortable with no noise, perfect for people who actually want to rest rather than party."

Room types and decor — Adrian View Resort has only about 7 rooms, a scale that makes the place feel very private, like staying at a relative's house · from the booking information there are several room types to choose from, such as the Deluxe Room (queen bed), Family Room (king bed) and Comfort Room for Four, which sleeps four for a group of friends or a family · the decor uses bright colours that many reviews say feel easy on the eye and keep the rooms from being as bland as the usual budget guesthouse · something a lot of people like is that every room has a private balcony or terrace with a small seating corner to step out, catch the breeze and sip a morning coffee · inside, the rooms have the standard guesthouse facilities — air conditioning, a flat-screen TV, a fridge, free drinking water, and bathroom amenities · the bathroom is private with a shower and a bidet spray · many reviews agree that the rooms are clean, the beds are comfortable, and it's quiet for a good sleep, with the sleep-quality scores drawing consistent praise · to be honest, because this is a small budget place, the rooms are simple, without gimmicks or fancy decorative touches, and some reviews use the words "basic" or "simple," which fits the price and the concept here · another thing to set the right expectation for is that the name includes the word View, but not every room has a wide, full sea view — many face the garden or the area around the house instead, so if you want a particular view, ask the owner directly when booking.

Facilities and common areas — let's be straight from the start: Adrian View Resort has no pool, gym, or spa like a big resort · what it has is a simplicity that fits a slow rest · the highlight of the common areas is a small, well-kept garden that reviews describe as a lovely garden courtyard with butterflies drifting around and a relaxed atmosphere, good for sitting out morning or evening · there is free private parking for anyone who brings a vehicle across (or parks on the Sriracha side and takes the ferry over), free Wi-Fi in the common areas, daily room service, a laundry service, and round-the-clock security · some listings also mention a VIP check-in service and a shared balcony/terrace corner to sit out in · the expectation to set right is that Adrian View is a place that leans toward "comfortable sleep, quiet, and privacy" rather than having activities or facilities to keep you busy all day · for people who come to Ko Si Chang to head out to the viewpoints and come back to rest, what's here is enough and in line with the price · but if you plan to spend the whole day at the property without going anywhere, you may find the in-house activities limited.

Food and breakfast — Adrian View Resort is a Bed & Breakfast, so it offers guests a simple breakfast, and TripAdvisor reviews state clearly that there's coffee, Ovaltine, toast, and sandwich spread in the morning · this isn't a big-hotel breakfast buffet, but a homestyle breakfast that fits the small-guesthouse concept, enough to start the morning comfortably before heading out · worth knowing: some booking channels list no breakfast service, but real reviews from past guests confirm a simple breakfast is provided, so if breakfast matters to you, ask the owner to confirm clearly when you book · for other meals, the place isn't far from the town and pier, so you can walk or take a skylab to reach the restaurants and seafood spots on the island · Ko Si Chang has plenty of seafood and made-to-order restaurants around the pier and in town, plus small cafes that welcome tourists · one thing to allow for is that many shops on the island close earlier than in the city, so if you plan to eat dinner out, head out early in the evening and check the closing times in advance · overall, food isn't Adrian View's main selling point, but the simple breakfast and a location within walking distance of the town's restaurants is enough for a short stay.

Service — service is the point that draws the heaviest praise in Adrian View's real reviews · what comes up again and again is the owner or manager being friendly and attentive, with several foreign reviews mentioning "the lady manageress" as lovely, smiling and genuinely helpful — with tips on places to visit, where to eat, and getting around the island · because it's a small place of just 7 rooms, guests feel looked after up close, like staying at a friend's house, rather than the formality of a big hotel · many people say they were warmly welcomed from the moment they arrived and given useful advice about exploring the island · the round-the-clock security and daily room service are details that help guests feel at ease too · to be fair, since this is a small owner-run place, some services may not run as precisely by the book as a chain hotel — things like responding to bookings or communication may take a direct call or a message via Facebook — but in terms of care and friendliness, this is Adrian View's clear strength.

What real reviews say (praise and gripes) — pulling together Trip.com (scored 8.5), TripAdvisor (4.3 out of 5 · ranked 4th of 11 Specialty stays on Ko Si Chang) and Booking.com, the picture is fairly consistent · on the praise side: the quiet and privacy that many people call the highlight, an owner and manager who are friendly and helpful, clean rooms with bright decor, comfortable sleep, the small garden with butterflies and a relaxed atmosphere, a location near the Khao Khat viewpoint and within walking distance of the pier, and value for money on a budget · on the gripes side: what comes up is that the rooms are very simple (basic/simple) with no gimmicks or fancy facilities, the place is small with only 7 rooms and limited facilities in the budget-stay style, there's no pool or in-house activities, and the room views aren't a wide sea view in every room as the name might lead you to expect · on top of that, the breakfast and facility details don't match across some booking channels, so it's best to ask the owner clearly before booking · most of these gripes are understandable for a budget place on a small island and can be managed by setting your expectations to match what this place is, rather than being big problems that leave people unimpressed.

"The room isn't fancy but it's clean and lovely, and the owner takes great care of you, like staying at a friend's house · good value, comfortable sleep, genuinely quiet · the only knock is the room is a touch too plain and there's no pool, but for this price and this atmosphere it's very okay, and I'll come back again."

Price comparison and value — Adrian View Resort's starting price is around ฿800/night in the budget range, climbing to about ฿1,300–1,500+ per night for a larger room such as the Family Room or Comfort Room for Four, or over weekends and long holidays · compared with other stays on Ko Si Chang, Adrian View falls into the budget guesthouse group, considerably cheaper than boutique resorts like Somewhere Koh Sichang or Sichang Palace · what you get back at this price is a clean, quiet room, an attentive owner, and a location near the Khao Khat viewpoint — which, for someone coming to Ko Si Chang to rest and visit the viewpoints, is worth the money · what makes it feel even better value is the homely, owner-run atmosphere, giving a warmer experience than many places at the same price · but if your goal is a pool, a wide sea view from the balcony, or a full set of resort facilities, this price reflects that the place doesn't offer those, and you should bump your budget up toward a boutique resort instead · overall, Adrian View is a place you pay for "quiet, cleanliness, and friendliness" on a budget, which fits travellers who come to Ko Si Chang without wanting to splurge.

Things to know before booking — a few things help the stay go more smoothly · one, since it's a small owner-run place, booking via Facebook or calling the owner directly (089-092-8652) usually gets you the clearest answers on availability, price, and breakfast, on top of booking through Trip.com or Booking.com · two, the breakfast and facility details don't match across some channels, so confirm with the owner whether breakfast is provided and what view your booked room has · three, if a view matters to you, ask specifically which room has the best view, because not every room sees a wide sea view · four, check the ferry timetable from Koh Loy Pier in Sriracha carefully, especially the last boat and long-weekend periods when the ferries can get full · five, plan dinner ahead, because many shops on the island close early and the place has no large dining room · six, if you're coming as a group or family, ask about the Comfort Room for Four, which sleeps four and works out better than booking several rooms · seven, the place has only 7 rooms, so it fills up fast over long holidays — book ahead.

The verdict — from all the real reviews, Adrian View Resort is the best fit for people who want to escape the city and sleep somewhere quiet on Ko Si Chang on a budget, with an attentive owner and a location near the Khao Khat viewpoint · being a small guesthouse of just 7 rooms, with clean, brightly coloured rooms, a balcony in every room, a small garden with butterflies, and a calm atmosphere, makes it a lovely choice among Ko Si Chang's budget stays, and the reason the review scores stay consistently good · if you're after a pool, a wide sea view from the balcony, a full set of facilities, or chain-hotel service, this may not be the answer, and you should consider a boutique resort like Somewhere Koh Sichang instead · but for a one-night, two-day trip where you want quiet, cleanliness, and the warm feeling of staying at a friend's house at an easy price — Adrian View Resort answers that nicely, and it's the reason many guests say they'll come back.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Adrian View Resort Ko Si Chang

faq.q: Where is Adrian View Resort, and how do you get there?
faq.a: The place is at 262/17 Moo 6, Tha Thaewawong, Ko Si Chang, Chonburi 20120, near the Khao Khat viewpoint · get there by driving or taking a coach to Koh Loy Pier in Sriracha (around 1.5–2 hours from Bangkok), then take the ferry across, around 50 baht, taking 45 min · once on the island, the place is about a 7 min walk or skylab ride from the pier.

faq.q: What's the starting price at Adrian View Resort, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at around ฿800/night for a Deluxe room in the budget range · there's a Family Room with a king bed, and a Comfort Room for Four that sleeps four for groups or families, with prices climbing to around ฿1,100–1,500+ depending on the room type and the season · the place has only 7 rooms, so book ahead, especially over long holidays.

faq.q: Who is Adrian View Resort right for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for couples, solo travellers, and budget travellers who want to escape the city and sleep somewhere quiet on Ko Si Chang · it leans into quiet, cleanliness, an attentive owner, and a location near the Khao Khat viewpoint · if you're after a pool, a wide sea view, or a full set of resort facilities, a boutique resort like Somewhere Koh Sichang may suit you better.

faq.q: Does Adrian View Resort have breakfast and a pool?
faq.a: The place is a Bed & Breakfast with a simple breakfast such as coffee, Ovaltine, toast and sandwiches, as real reviews note · but there's no pool, because it's a small guesthouse that keeps things simple · the breakfast details don't match across some booking channels, so ask the owner clearly before booking.

faq.q: What should you know about Adrian View Resort before booking?
faq.a: From real reviews, what to know is that the rooms are very simple, with no gimmicks or fancy facilities · there's no pool or in-house activities · the room views aren't a wide sea view in every room · and you have to take the ferry across, so check the last boat carefully · it's best to call or message the owner on Facebook to confirm the details before booking.

faq.q: How do you book Adrian View Resort, and how do you get in touch?
faq.a: You can book through Trip.com and Booking.com, or contact the owner directly by phone on 089-092-8652 or via the Facebook page "Adrian View Resort" · since it's a small owner-run place, contacting them directly usually gets you the clearest information on availability, price, and breakfast.
